chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad ibn Isa from Shu'ayb from Abu Basir who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man buys a female slave while she is pure (not menstruating), and her owner claims that he has not had sexual intercourse with her since she menstruated. He (the Imam) said: 'If you trust him, then he has had intercourse with her.'
And it is more precautionary to observe her waiting period (istibra') in all cases. Sam'ah narrated that in the narration we presented earlier, and also he has narrated it.

key_terms.اسْتِبْرَاءُهَا: Observing her waiting period to confirm non-pregnancy

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a female slave's pregnancy status when her owner claims he has not had intercourse with her?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *istibra'* (waiting period) for female slaves to ensure lineage purity (*luluq al-awlad*), balancing reliance on the owner's testimony with legal caution. It reflects the Shia juristic approach to verifying paternity in slave ownership, where the Imam advises that while trust in the owner is sufficient for immediate intercourse, observing the waiting period is the more prudent (*ahwat*) course to prevent disputes over offspring.
